questions.question_text: A quantity satisfying $\dfrac{dQ}{dt}=0.08Q$ is modelled by $Q=250e^{0.08t}$, with $t$ in years. Find $Q$ when $t=15$ years, correct to the nearest whole number.

options.why: Used linear growth $250(1+0.08\times 15)$ instead of the exponential model.
Multiplied $250$ by the index $1.2$ rather than by $e^{1.2}$.
Used $e^{-1.2}$, treating a growth model as decay.

questions.question_text: A sample decays according to $M=90e^{-0.15t}$ grams after $t$ hours. Find the time at which $M=30$ grams, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Divided $\ln\frac{1}{3}$ by $0.15$ instead of by $-0.15$, giving a negative time.
Used $\ln 2$ instead of $\ln 3$, solving for a halving rather than a fall to one third.
Divided $0.15$ by $\ln 3$ instead of $\ln 3$ by $0.15$.

questions.question_text: A substance satisfies $\dfrac{dQ}{dt}=-0.11Q$, with $t$ in years. Find its half-life, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Computed $\dfrac{1}{0.11}$, leaving out the factor $\ln 2$.
Halved the correct time, on the mistaken idea that a half-life must be halved.
Doubled the correct time, confusing half-life with doubling time.

questions.question_text: A quantity satisfies $\dfrac{dQ}{dt}=kQ$, with $Q=5000$ at $t=0$ and $Q=2000$ after $4$ hours. Find $k$, correct to $4$ decimal places.

options.why: Took $k$ as positive although the quantity is decaying, using $\ln 2.5$ instead of $\ln 0.4$.
Found $4k$ but never divided by the $4$ hours.
Took $k$ as positive for decay and also never divided by the $4$ hours.

questions.question_text: A quantity satisfies $\dfrac{dQ}{dt}=0.07Q$, where $Q$ is in litres and $t$ in hours. Find the rate of change of $Q$ at the moment when $Q=4500$ litres.

options.why: Used $k=0.007$, slipping one decimal place.
Divided $Q$ by $k$ instead of multiplying.
Added $0.07Q$ to $Q$, giving the new amount rather than the rate.

questions.question_text: A tank of liquid satisfies $\dfrac{dV}{dt}=-0.3V$ with $V=2400$ litres at $t=0$, where $t$ is in hours. Find the volume after $6$ hours, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Used $e^{1.8}$ instead of $e^{-1.8}$, treating decay as growth.
Subtracted the correct final volume from the initial volume, reporting the change instead.
Multiplied $2400$ by $0.3$, using the constant of proportionality as a fraction remaining.

questions.question_text: A population satisfies $\dfrac{dP}{dt}=kP$, with $P=900$ when $t=2$ years and $P=2700$ when $t=7$ years. Find $k$, correct to $4$ decimal places.

options.why: Divided $\ln 3$ by the later time $7$ instead of by the $5$-year gap.
Divided $\ln 3$ by the earlier time $2$ instead of by the $5$-year gap.
Added the two times to get $10$ instead of subtracting them to get the $5$-year gap.

questions.question_text: A population satisfies $\dfrac{dP}{dt}=0.05P$ with $P=12\,000$ at $t=0$, where $t$ is in years. Find the time at which the population reaches $30\,000$, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Found the doubling time using $\ln 2$ rather than the $\ln 2.5$ this increase needs.
Divided $2.5$ by $0.05$ without taking logarithms first.
Used $\ln 5$ instead of $\ln 2.5$, from $\dfrac{30\,000}{12\,000}$ miscomputed as $5$.
